userStories.title: nax unit test hygiene
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make nax's 21 failing unit-test files portable to the confined runner and expose that runner through reusable test helpers and test:confined.

**Motivation** — All but about a dozen of the 194 failures are a write under a literal `/tmp/...` path, which a confined session denies by design (nax#2301).

**Approach** — **Confined test runner (nax#2523).** A nax-agent script runs `bun test <paths>` inside the same OS sandbox a confined agent session gets. It builds the policy with `buildSandboxPolicy({ confined: true, ... })`, wraps the command with the srt backend, and exports `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` (the session temp dir under the run's own temp root) plus `NAX_TEST_CONFINED=1`. It is the regression gate for test temp hygiene: a test that writes under a literal `/tmp/...` path fails there exactly as it fails in an agent session, while a test that uses `makeTempDir()` (which resolves through `os.tmpdir()`, and so through `$TMPDIR`) passes. Each package gets a `test:confined` script, and CI runs it over `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` after the existing bubblewrap install step. The runner lives in `packages/nax-agent/scripts/`, not `packages/repo-tooling/scripts/`, because it imports nax-agent's own `src/sandbox` (repo-tooling may not import a package's `src/`). The runner itself is US-001; the nax CI step is US-003.

The file lists in US-001, US-002 and US-003 are exhaustive for main `0bf6cef38`: the census ran every file under `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` of both packages inside the confined sandbox. A failure a story finds outside its list (a test added since) is fixed the same way, within the same story.

Failing tests are fixed by class:
- **Class A — the test makes its own temp dir or lock file under a literal `/tmp/...`.** Use `makeTempDir()` / `withTempDir()` / `cleanupTempDir()` from the package's `test/helpers`.
- **Class B — a "fake" fixture path the code under test actually writes** (for example `prdPath: "/tmp/test-prd.json"` reaching `savePRD`, which writes `/tmp/test-prd.json.tmp-<uuid>`). Point the fixture at a real temp dir, or stub the write through the module's existing `_deps` seam. These writes also leak into the host's `/tmp` on every ordinary run today.
- **Class C — the behaviour itself needs something a confined sandbox withholds** (a nested sandbox, a detached process probe, the shared `/tmp/nax` parent). Fix the test when its expectation is merely environment-dependent. Otherwise mark it `test.skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())`, with a comment that names what the sandbox withholds.

The `.nax/scratchpad/` directory is the agent's own notes space, written through the Scratchpad tools. It is not a home for test fixtures: tests run on hosts and in CI too, and the test-side counterpart of the sandbox's own "use $TMPDIR or .nax/scratchpad/, not /tmp" guidance is `$TMPDIR`.

Each `test:confined` script mirrors its package's normal test phases as separate runner invocations, so a confined-only failure is never an artefact of mixing directories in one `bun test` process. nax: `bun ../nax-agent/scripts/run-confined-tests.ts --package=. --timeout=5000 ./test/unit/ && bun ../nax-agent/scripts/run-confined-tests.ts --package=. --timeout=5000 ./test/integration/` (5 s per test, as `scripts/run-tests-phases.ts` uses).

**Interface** — `isConfinedTestRun(): boolean`, `confinedSandboxAvailable(): Promise<boolean>`, `runConfinedFiles(paths: readonly string[]): Promise<number>` in packages/nax/test/helpers/confined.ts. These spawn `bun ../nax-agent/scripts/run-confined-tests.ts --package=<packages/nax> ...` (with `--probe` for availability). Also adds the `test:confined` script (two invocations at `--timeout=5000`, unit then integration; see Design) and `test/integration/confined/unit-hygiene.test.ts`. Add the helper exports to test/helpers/index.ts. isConfinedTestRun is a sanctioned copy of nax-agent's helper, with a first-line note naming the original; it reads NAX_TEST_CONFINED=1. The runner CLI is `bun scripts/run-confined-tests.ts [--package=<dir>] [--timeout=<ms>] [--probe] <test paths...>` and its exit codes are 0/test failure codes, SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE_EXIT=3 and USAGE_EXIT=2. `runConfinedFiles` resolves the runner's exit code unchanged; a failure to spawn `bun` rejects. Do not pre-probe []: it must reach usage 2 without requiring a sandbox.

Fix all these test/unit/<name>.test.ts files, preserving every assertion's meaning:
- Class A: execution/pid-registry, metrics/save-run-metrics, ui/tui-controls, utils/queue-file-lock, bakeoff/coordinator, bakeoff/preflight, bakeoff/report.
- Class B (fake PRD/workdir paths that get written): execution/pipeline-result-handler, execution/pipeline-result-handler-bug12, execution/pipeline-result-handler-worktree-cleanup, execution/unified-executor-cost, execution/unified-executor-dispatch, execution/unified-executor-failure, execution/unified-executor-fallback-seam, execution/unified-executor-results, execution/escalation/tier-escalation-retry-cap, execution/structured-failure, pipeline/stages/acceptance-setup-gate.
- Class C: agents/coding-tool-support-session-tmp, agents/coding-tool-support-command-shadow, agent-runtime/bun-runtime.

Integration hygiene commands skip when confinedSandboxAvailable() is false or isConfinedTestRun() is true to avoid nested sandbox launches; ordinary class A/B test behavior remains exercised in a confined suite. Tests that assert persistence use a real temp path; only incidental writes may be intercepted through existing seams. Runner/backend changes belong to US-001.

**Scope** — In: nax helper and barrel, new helper/unit-hygiene tests, package script and 21 enumerated unit fixture repairs. Out: runner implementation and nax-agent hygiene/CI (US-001), nax integration fixture repairs and CI job (US-003), re-review findings (US-004), telemetry (US-005), workflow reviewer prompts (US-006). Moving test fixtures into `.nax/scratchpad/` — the scratchpad is the agent's own notes space; tests use `$TMPDIR` through `makeTempDir()`. Changing the confined-session sandbox policy itself (the `/tmp` deny, the run temp roots, network rules) — this spec makes tests fit the policy, never the reverse. Making `ps` or other setuid programs runnable inside the macOS sandbox, and making a sandbox launch inside another sandbox work — tests that need either are skipped in a confined run instead. A static lint for literal `/tmp/` strings in tests — most such strings are harmless path values that are never written; the confined CI run is the gate. Running the confined runner over `test/ui/` or `test/e2e/` — only `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` are covered.

userStories.title: nax integration test hygiene and the CI gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Repair nax's 17 confined-failing integration fixture files and enforce unit/integration confinement in nax CI.

**Motivation** — So an agent session can never run the suite or the coverage gate, and every reviewer writes "could not run the full suite" as a `cannotVerify`.

**Approach** — **Confined test runner (nax#2523).** A nax-agent script runs `bun test <paths>` inside the same OS sandbox a confined agent session gets. It builds the policy with `buildSandboxPolicy({ confined: true, ... })`, wraps the command with the srt backend, and exports `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP` (the session temp dir under the run's own temp root) plus `NAX_TEST_CONFINED=1`. The runner lives in `packages/nax-agent/scripts/`, not `packages/repo-tooling/scripts/`, because it imports nax-agent's own `src/sandbox` (repo-tooling may not import a package's `src/`).

The file lists in US-001, US-002 and US-003 are exhaustive for main `0bf6cef38`: the census ran every file under `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` of both packages inside the confined sandbox. A failure a story finds outside its list (a test added since) is fixed the same way, within the same story.

Failing tests are fixed by class:
- **Class A — the test makes its own temp dir or lock file under a literal `/tmp/...`.** Use `makeTempDir()` / `withTempDir()` / `cleanupTempDir()` from the package's `test/helpers`.
- **Class B — a "fake" fixture path the code under test actually writes** (for example `prdPath: "/tmp/test-prd.json"` reaching `savePRD`, which writes `/tmp/test-prd.json.tmp-<uuid>`). Point the fixture at a real temp dir, or stub the write through the module's existing `_deps` seam. These writes also leak into the host's `/tmp` on every ordinary run today.
- **Class C — the behaviour itself needs something a confined sandbox withholds** (a nested sandbox, a detached process probe, the shared `/tmp/nax` parent). Fix the test when its expectation is merely environment-dependent. Otherwise mark it `test.skipIf(isConfinedTestRun())`, with a comment that names what the sandbox withholds.

The `.nax/scratchpad/` directory is the agent's own notes space, written through the Scratchpad tools. It is not a home for test fixtures: tests run on hosts and in CI too, and the test-side counterpart of the sandbox's own "use $TMPDIR or .nax/scratchpad/, not /tmp" guidance is `$TMPDIR`.

Each `test:confined` script mirrors its package's normal test phases as separate runner invocations, so a confined-only failure is never an artefact of mixing directories in one `bun test` process. nax: `bun ../nax-agent/scripts/run-confined-tests.ts --package=. --timeout=5000 ./test/unit/ && bun ../nax-agent/scripts/run-confined-tests.ts --package=. --timeout=5000 ./test/integration/` (5 s per test, as `scripts/run-tests-phases.ts` uses). The wall-clock bound in CI is the job's `timeout-minutes`; each story raises its job's value if the added confined step needs it.

**Interface** — Consume the US-002 helpers `isConfinedTestRun(): boolean`, `confinedSandboxAvailable(): Promise<boolean>` and `runConfinedFiles(paths: readonly string[]): Promise<number>` from test/helpers, using the US-001 runner CLI end to end. Adds `test/integration/confined/integration-hygiene.test.ts` and a "Test (confined sandbox)" step (`bun run test:confined`) in the CI `nax` job, after its bubblewrap install step. Fixes the 17 integration files that fail confined:
- Class A/B: execution/execution, execution/runner-parallel-metrics, execution/runner-parallel-metrics-rectification-events, execution/runner-fixes, execution/checkpoint/reader, execution/progress, plan/plan, plan/analyze-scanner, context/context-integration, config/security-loader, tdd/story-orchestrator-core, tdd/story-orchestrator-failureCategory, tdd/story-orchestrator-fallback, interaction/interaction-chain-pipeline, worktree/manager.
- Class C: permissions/bash-deny-suite (launches a sandbox, so it nests) and execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe (asserts the shared `/tmp/nax` parent).
Each is `test/integration/<name>.test.ts`. Keep every assertion's meaning. For class C add explicit skip comments naming the nested sandbox/shared parent; preserve ordinary host assertions and sandbox policy. Every child-run hygiene assertion is skipped when confinedSandboxAvailable() is false or isConfinedTestRun() is true. Check isConfinedTestRun() before performing the availability probe, so a confined invocation launches neither child suites nor a nested --probe process. Do not turn a CI sandbox absence into success: CI runs test:confined and fails on nonzero exit, including 3. routing.reasoning: New pure abstraction consumed by two persisted state machines, parser/prompt contract extension, artifact filtering and log compatibility; no new authorization mechanism.

suggestedCriteria: parseReReviewReply omits a residual when PARTIAL carries a whitespace-only issue or a non-object residual.
parseReReviewReply omits empty suggestion/file strings and negative, fractional or nonnumeric residual lines.
parseReReviewReply ignores a residual supplied on an ADDRESSED or unknown verdict value.
absorbReReviewVerdict preserves asked order and does not mutate asked findings or the parsed verdict.
absorbReReviewVerdict retains every draft when a residual finding's effective line is absent.
When a PARTIAL duplicate draft has minor severity, runStoryLoop does not append it to the deferred-minor ledger.
When a branch PARTIAL duplicate draft is dropped, branch-rereview.json contains no assigned blocker or non-blocking duplicate at that location.
When branch re-review leaves a fix-now minor unaddressed, its triage becomes leave without adding it to reviewOpen.

modifiedFiles.reason: asserts the branch re-review prompt contains the two-value verdict contract; the contract now lists three values, so the assertion becomes that the prompt contains the three-value contract `ADDRESSED|PARTIAL|NOT_ADDRESSED`.

routing.reasoning: Usage-field aggregation/presentation spans multiple modules and CI progress adds clock-dependent polling and publish lifecycle assertions; cache token counts are not security credentials and the logging changes do not alter approval or session access decisions, so isolated lite TDD is sufficient.

userStories.title: Workflow reviewers see nax's gate results
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Pass recorded story/repository gate results into workflow review prompts and narrow cannotVerify to genuine verification gaps.

**Motivation** — So "full suite not re-run" reads to the reviewer as a real gap.

**Approach** — **Reviewers see nax's gate results (nax#2527).** The workflow story review gets the story's gate states, and the branch review gets the repo-gate summary. Both prompts get a "What nax already checked" block that states those results and the gates that run after the review. They expect a scoped run of the story's own tests when a shell tool is available, and they limit `cannotVerify` to what neither nax's gates nor a scoped command can check. The shared `reviewerCommandsSection()` (also used by pipeline-mode reviewers) is unchanged.

**Interface** — `StoryLoopSteps.storyReview` in packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts — Target: `storyReview(concerns: readonly string[], gates?: Readonly<Partial<Record<GateName, GateState>>>)`; `runStoryReview(sc, concerns, gates = {})` in story-review.ts and the `buildStoryEnv` wiring in stage-env.ts follow. The parameter is optional so every existing two-argument caller and fake keeps compiling.

`buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt(input)` in packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-story-review-builder.ts — Target: input gains `readonly gates?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"lint" | "typecheck" | "scoped" | "full-suite", "green" | "red" | "skipped">>>` (a local structural type, so the prompt builders keep importing nothing from `@/workflow`); absent means `{}` (every gate `not run`).

`BranchReviewPromptInput` in packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts — Target: gains `readonly repoGates?: { readonly ran: readonly string[]; readonly failing: readonly string[] }` (structurally `RepoGateSummary`, declared locally for the same layering reason); `BranchReviewFacts` (branch-review.ts) picks it too, and `reviewFacts` in feature-machine.ts sets it from `rec.repoGates`.

Story review block, inserted before the verdict instructions:
> ## What nax already checked
> nax ran these gates on this story before your review: lint <state>, typecheck <state>, scoped tests <state>.
> After your review nax runs the full test suite on this story, and once every story is done it runs the repository gates. Do not list any of these as something you could not verify.
> If you have a shell tool, run this story's own test files with one scoped test command before you give the spec verdict.

`<state>` is `green`, `red`, `skipped`, or `not run` when the gate has no state.

Story and branch `cannotVerify` sentence. It replaces "Put anything you could not check in \"cannotVerify\".":
> Put in "cannotVerify" only what neither nax's gates nor a scoped command can check, such as behaviour that needs a live external service.

Branch review block:
> ## What nax already checked
> Repository gates before this review: <ran, comma-separated, or "not run">; failing: <failing, comma-separated, or "none">.
> nax runs them again after the branch fix. Do not list any of these as something you could not verify.

Wire runStoryLoop's s.gates.states into storyReview as the second argument, forwarding through buildStoryEnv's timed/toolErrors adapters to runStoryReview and the builder. Pass rec.repoGates through reviewFacts → BranchReviewFacts → runBranchReview → the branch builder. Do not import workflow types into prompt builders; use the given local structural declarations. Story gates with no recorded state render not run, not green. A feature record with no repoGates renders exactly `Repository gates before this review: not run; failing: none.` Existing gateless calls in reviews.test.ts, reviews-hardening.test.ts and workflow-builders.test.ts retain behavior/compilation; no existing test pins the replaced cannotVerify sentence. Add entry-point assertions for runStoryLoop and runFeatureMachine as well as _workflowDeps.callOp prompt checks.

**Scope** — In: workflow story and branch normal-review prompt context/data flow, exact gate/scoped-test instructions and narrowed cannotVerify sentence. Out: confinement/test fixtures (US-001..US-003), PARTIAL re-review contracts/absorption (US-004), cache/publish telemetry (US-005). Changing `reviewerCommandsSection()` or any pipeline-mode (non-workflow) reviewer prompt. Including the gate command lines in the review prompts — the story gate record holds states, not commands.

Also adds, to both workflow review prompts, the evidence rule for unavailability claims (nax#2531): "Say a tool or service is unavailable only together with the command you ran and the error it returned; otherwise say what you did not try."

routing.reasoning: Existing gate states and repo summaries only need optional parameter/facts forwarding through established wrappers plus local prompt rendering; standard failing-first tests at the builders and state-machine seams cover this additive change without a new abstraction or security decision.

analysis:
Goal and completion: close #2523, #2524, #2525, #2526 and #2527 by making confined test execution a real CI/developer gate, preserving one finding identity across partial fixes, accounting for cache traffic in workflow role telemetry, making publishing observable, and teaching workflow reviewers which checks nax already performs. This is an enhancement to an existing Bun-workspace TypeScript monorepo, not a new workflow engine. No implementation or runtime validation was performed during PRD drafting. Codebase-memory MCP was unavailable, so discovery used direct reads and text searches; the census failure totals and exhaustive file lists are spec evidence, not independently rerun results. The supplied census is for main 0bf6cef38; additional failures from tests introduced since that revision should be repaired by the same class in the applicable hygiene story.

Repository conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:16 identifies the DI/error/constants conventions; :23 identifies async, test and structured logging rules; :82 describes runtime/operation boundaries; :96 identifies prompt construction as its own layer. The architecture index is at the repository root, not packages/nax/docs (that package-relative read did not exist). packages/nax-agent/CLAUDE.md:115 requires runtimeSpawn/getAgentRuntime().spawn, :126 requires #src imports rather than nax aliases, :149 requires external-call _deps seams, and :158 confines helpers to test/helpers and requires demonstrating a regression test fails on old code. Shipped nax-agent source is Node-compatible; nax is Bun-native. Do not import another package's src from repo-tooling or expose script/test helpers on nax-agent's public API. The existing API surface and lockstep versions need no change. The new runner belongs in nax-agent/scripts, with injectable I/O, and nax reaches it by CLI rather than cross-package source imports. No change is needed in nax-ai, nax-agent-acp or cost calculation.

Binding structure and execution: exactly US-001 through US-006 with the specified package workdirs. The final binding table says Depends on '(not stated)' for every story, overriding the earlier narrative dependency lists; dependencies are therefore [] for every story. Nevertheless US-002 operationally consumes US-001's CLI and US-003 consumes US-002's helper, so execute these stories in listed workflow order; parallel execution before those outputs exist will fail. To avoid missing-context warnings, contextFiles lists only files existing today, not these undeclared upstream outputs. US-001 and US-003 retain their binding package workdirs despite editing the root .github/workflows/ci.yml as explicit exceptions. Both stories edit the same CI file and must preserve the other's step. US-004 and US-006 both edit story-loop.ts, feature-machine.ts and workflow-branch-builder.ts; US-005 shares workflow/types.ts. Preserve the preceding story's changes. 'Modifies: None' in the first hygiene stories means no preexisting assertion contract changes, not that their named test files, helper barrels, manifests or CI cannot be edited. The security override applies to sandbox/access-control/session work; telemetry cache token fields are usage counts, not credentials, and must never trigger token inspection or a new authentication path.

US-001 architecture and impact: packages/nax-agent/src/coding-tools/coding-tool-sandbox.ts:102 resolves session sandbox support; :144 builds a policy using resolved git layout, git guard files, credential files, discovered .nax entries, temp roots and platform. It creates the session temp directory before granting its roots and distinguishes resolved confinement from per-command TMPDIR availability. Reuse the policy inputs, not this session adapter's fail-open fallback: the confined runner must return 3 and never run unsandboxed when unavailable. packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/policy-builder.ts:26 declares SandboxPolicyInput; :154 builds literal/realpathed roots and denies; :73 canonicalizes every policy path using realOrRaw. packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/policy-inputs.ts:34 resolves worktree versus main git layouts, :48 enumerates .nax entries, :58 enumerates credentials, and :83 excludes shared /tmp and /private/tmp from runTempRoots. packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/srt-backend.ts:49 creates the backend; :75 wraps commands; :98 commandFinished decrements in-flight work and cleans placeholders; :104 reset clears the singleton state. packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/probe.ts:26 actually runs a wrapped command and checks enforcement, not mere bwrap installation; :49 calls commandFinished after the probe. packages/nax-agent/src/runtime/types.ts:9 requires stdout='pipe', :27 gives a ReadableStream stdout and exit promise, and :52 exposes synchronous spawn. The runner must concurrently drain stdout to the injectable output stream and await exit, inherit stdin/stderr, use precisely the backend argv, create <root>/s before wrap, and clean up command state and its unique root after execution. The policy retains Claude settings denies and credential protections; don't broaden temporary permissions to repair tests. The root's unique /tmp/nax/confined-<pid>-<random> name must not be confused with fixtures under TMPDIR. Probe-only mode must not run tests or prepare a test policy; CLI validation precedes probing.

US-001 test evidence: packages/nax-agent/test/unit/internal/file-lock.test.ts:32 and path-file-lock.test.ts:27 construct literal /tmp lock directories. Replace only directory setup/cleanup, preserving lock behaviour. packages/nax-agent/test/unit/runtime/node-runtime.test.ts:6 iterates SPAWN_CASES; packages/test-kit/src/cases/spawn-cases.ts:220 identifies the ps-based detached process-group probe. Skip only environment-dependent cases in the consumer, not the shared cases or production spawn implementation. packages/nax-agent/test/helpers/index.ts:20 already exports portable temp helpers. New writes-literal-tmp.fixture.ts must fail confined while writes-tmpdir.fixture.ts passes; these are explicit ./ fixture paths with a non-test suffix, never normally collected. Real sandbox integration tests skip unavailable hosts and confined invocations to prevent nested sandboxes, but the package's CI confined command fails if the runner returns 3. packages/nax-agent/package.json:29 has separate unit/integration invocations at 60s; mirror this precisely. .github/workflows/ci.yml:119 starts the nax-agent job with timeout-minutes 10; :149 installs bubblewrap/socat/ripgrep and relaxes AppArmor. Add the confined step after that install and raise the job bound only if needed, leaving normal unit/integration and coverage steps intact.

US-002/US-003 portable fixtures and CLI integration: packages/nax/test/helpers/temp.ts:2 reexports the shared temp library; packages/test-kit/src/bun/temp.ts:32 calls mkdtempSync(join(os.tmpdir(), prefix)), :42 removes fixtures, and :62 provides try/finally async cleanup. These already honor TMPDIR; no new temp-root system or scratchpad fixtures are necessary. packages/nax/test/helpers/index.ts:1 is the helper barrel. Add a first-line provenance note to the sanctioned isConfinedTestRun copy and expose availability and exit-code helpers through the barrel. The helpers invoke bun and the nax-agent runner with an absolute package dir, probe with --probe, preserve every exit code, and reject spawn failure rather than translating it to a sandbox absence. Do not probe before forwarding []: usage 2 must be observable on hosts without a sandbox. Existing source seams should intercept incidental writes only where persistence is not the subject of the assertion; real persistence assertions need genuine temp-backed paths. packages/nax/test/unit/execution/pipeline-result-handler.test.ts:71 has fake /tmp/prd.json and /tmp/repo defaults; :116 restores seams around calls. packages/nax/src/prd/index.ts:147 savePRD delegates to saveJsonFile, so those fake paths are not just strings; an unstubbed path leaks a real atomic write. packages/nax/test/integration/execution/runner-fixes.test.ts:312 has literal /tmp PRD fixtures. packages/nax/test/integration/worktree/manager.test.ts:32 already makes a portable git fixture; other fake handler paths in this long file must be audited without changing its genuine worktree assertions. packages/nax/test/integration/execution/lifecycle/run-tmp-wipe.test.ts:25 documents the literal shared /tmp/nax parent and :78 creates it through runtime helpers; preserve its host assertion and skip confined execution rather than weakening production cleanup. Environment-dependent nested sandbox, detached ps and shared-parent probes may be skipped with a comment naming the withheld facility; don't blanket-skip class A/B tests. All 21 unit files and 17 integration files enumerated in the story descriptions remain in their original story and preserve each assertion's meaning. Their aggregate child-run tests must skip before attempting nested sandbox launches. packages/nax/scripts/run-tests-phases.ts:14 defines separate phases, :20 keeps the normal per-test timeout at 5000, and :30 places e2e outside normal execution. packages/nax/package.json:49 runs the phase wrapper and :53 shows the same 5s per-test normal layout. The new confined script covers only unit and integration as separate 5s invocations, not ui/e2e. .github/workflows/ci.yml:27 starts the nax job with timeout-minutes 15 and :61 installs bubblewrap; add only the confined step and adjust its wall-clock bound if needed. Existing CI normal test steps intentionally use 60s, whereas this spec's confined phases mirror the developer wrapper's 5s; do not silently replace either timeout.

US-004 finding identity and layering: packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-types.ts:50 currently has boolean-addressed verdict entries only; operations owns reply types because workflow depends on operations, not the reverse (:1). packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-replies.ts:28 preserves nonempty original strings, :73 sanitizes drafts including positive integer lines, and :123 parseReReviewReply maps requested ids in order, ignores duplicate id entries after the first, fails closed on missing verdicts, and currently recognizes only ADDRESSED. Add optional sanitized residual only for PARTIAL without changing the boolean contract or closed-world shape otherwise. packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:2 already reexports operation types; the new pure re-review-absorb.ts can consume the workflow type facade and must not import @/operations or @/prompts. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:201 currently computes stillOpen from verdicts and :203 defers raw newFindings, allowing duplicates into blockers and ledger minors. Replace both paths with one absorption result before assigning ids or deferring anything. :211 pins the existing per-id summary wording. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:250 mixes blockers with fix-now minors in the re-review request; :269 fails closed on omitted verdicts, :272 assigns raw drafts, :273 writes branch artifacts, :277 changes unresolved fix-now minors to leave, and :290 performs the optional second-fix eligibility check. Absorb only rec.reviewOpen; keep minor triage based on the original verdicts/items and preserve the second-round eligibility rule from :112. A residual must keep its id and severity/kind/acId, replace only sanitized supplied fields, drop observed proof of the old issue, and use its effective file+line for exact duplicate suppression. Missing either location means no suppression; no fuzzy matching. Story rereview artifacts keep the parsed reply; branch artifacts keep assigned blocking ids plus unassigned minors from filtered drafts. Without residuals, story and branch summaries must remain byte-for-byte identical. Tests at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-machine-log.test.ts:78 already capture the whole feature state machine; corresponding story-loop-log, story-loop, feature-machine and operations/workflow-replies tests cover entry points and parsing. packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/workflow-branch-builder.test.ts:80 pins ADDRESSED|NOT_ADDRESSED and is the one preexisting contract assertion explicitly changed to three values. Prompt builders are packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-re-review-builder.ts:4 and workflow-branch-builder.ts:71.

US-005 additive telemetry and observable publishing: packages/nax/src/workflow/tokens.ts:5 defines structural MeterEvent, :22 EMPTY_TOKENS has the old four-key shape, :24 add drops cache fields, :33 addRoleTokens combines records, and :41 startTokenMeter only copies uncached input/output and costs. Extend both event reading and accumulation, emitting each cache key only when its total is nonzero; preserve uncached inputTokens, exactCostUsd preference and calls. packages/nax/src/workflow/types.ts:112 persists RoleTokens and :89 includes preflight role records. packages/nax/src/workflow/run-summary.ts:19 already combines story, feature and preflight records through addRoleTokens and spreads totals into role entries; it needs no parallel recomputation from the ledger. packages/nax/src/log-format/types.ts:67 supplies WorkflowRoleUsage; workflow-summary.ts:27 formats role lines and currently has no cache suffix. Backward records with absent fields read as zero and retain the previous shape/output. packages/nax/src/workflow/ci-wait.ts:47 classifies GitHub pass/skipping as green while tolerating nonzero gh status with parseable output, :60 reads GitLab head_pipeline/pipeline, :81 catches CLI failures as pending, and :91 waitForChecks returns green/failed/pending with details and respects AbortSignal/deadline. Add summary information/progress without changing those semantics; log start before the first poll, changed summaries only, a 60000ms info heartbeat since the last info line, and an end line on terminal returns. Use existing formatDuration and getSafeLogger; no installed logger must remain harmless. Logging data has storyId:'_run' inserted first for renderer grouping. packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:62 handles the main push, :181 finishPr promotes or preserves draft, :274 pushMode waits without PR operations, :288 prMode opens draft/waits/asks approval, and :316 publish selects modes and protects dry-run/main/no-forge paths. Add truthful success lines only after success and retain exceptions, readiness reasons, already-ready handling and push-failure local-only outcomes. Do not add progress to ledgerCommit (:220), pushLedger (:238), or mode none. Existing finalize.test.ts:83 wire stubs ledger, forge, CI and approval-related paths, allowing deterministic log verification; ci-wait.test.ts, tokens.test.ts, run-summary.test.ts and log-format workflow summary tests are the regression anchors.

US-006 workflow-only review context: packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:33 exposes storyReview(concerns), :177 calls it without gates, and :234 stores s.gates.states before review, so the data is already present and must be passed as the optional second argument, not recomputed or fabricated. packages/nax/src/workflow/stage-env.ts:115 wraps storyReview in timing/tool-error adapters and :116 invokes runStoryReview; both must forward the optional gates. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-review.ts:56 builds the prompt and calls _workflowDeps.callOp; supply gates={} by default. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-story-review-builder.ts:3 has a local input shape and :26 has the broad cannotVerify instruction; add the local structural optional states type, state renderings and exact gate/scoped-test text before verdict instructions. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:139 builds branch facts but omits existing rec.repoGates; :159 stores the repo summary and :191 passes facts to branchReview. packages/nax/src/workflow/branch-review.ts:18 derives BranchReviewFacts via Pick and :35 spreads those facts into the builder; include repoGates in that pick and data flow. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts:9 owns a local BranchReviewPromptInput, :34 builds the whole-branch prompt, and :65 currently uses the broad cannotVerify sentence. Keep prompt builders free of @/workflow imports using the specified structural types. No command strings are recorded by story gates, so show actual states, including skipped/red/not run, not invented commands or a blanket claim of green. Scope expectation is conditional on shell availability and does not pretend the reviewer executed checks; cannotVerify remains available for live external service behaviour. Existing workflow reviews/reviews-hardening tests and workflow-builders/branch-builder tests must continue accepting gateless calls; reviewerCommandsSection and all pipeline-mode reviewer prompts remain untouched.

Migration and verification risks: all new persistent/cache/residual fields and gate arguments are optional, result schema version stays 1, old booleans and role-record shapes still parse, and no data migration/backfill is required. Missing gates render 'not run', missing repo summaries render 'not run; failing: none', and malformed PARTIAL fails closed without mutating an issue. The main risks are accidentally widening sandbox permissions, deadlocking piped stdout, leaked backend state/temp roots, skipping tests too broadly, replacing tests' real persistence assertions with meaningless stubs, double-assigning residual drafts, erasing fix-now minor handling, changing legacy log strings, emitting undefined/zero cache keys in closed-world records, and mistaking unchanged CI poll summaries for progress. Use existing shared fixtures and _deps restoration, deterministic clocks for heartbeat tests, and entry-point tests at runStoryLoop/runFeatureMachine/publish rather than only helper tests. Regression evidence must be red against old code; new-import tests can first prove failure via absent APIs under the chosen TDD strategy. Real sandbox tests are allowed to skip unavailable development hosts, but neither CI's test:confined command nor a runner invocation may silently fall back. The feature is complete when the confined CI scripts enforce policy with repaired fixtures, partial residuals remain single actionable items, cache telemetry preserves uncached semantics, CI waits stay visible, and workflow review prompts accurately carry the previously recorded gate results without changing pipeline reviewers.

Refine-pass adversarial audit: all 111 original spec acceptance criteria remain in their original stories. Inventory checked in spec order: US-001 (23): run-root grant; shared-root exclusion; same-session Claude settings deny; command prefix; command suffix; explicit/default timeout; unavailable exit/no spawn; unavailable stderr; exit 1; every stdout chunk; exact backend argv; mkdir before wrap; nonzero cleanup; cleanup-error exit unchanged; commandFinished then reset; nongit fallback; env helper true; usage exit/text; probe availability codes; literal tmp denied; TMPDIR allowed; lock files green; runtime file green. The timeout, unavailable/no-spawn and usage/text compound criteria are split into independent assertions without dropping either half. US-002 (14): env true/false; probe exit exactly; empty paths usage without sandbox; pid; metrics; tui/queue; bakeoff group; pipeline-handler group; executor group; escalation/structured failure; acceptance setup; session tmp; command shadow; Bun runtime. True/false is split; every shared unavailable/confined qualifier is attached to its child-run assertion. outOfScope: Making `ps` or other setuid programs runnable inside the macOS sandbox, and making a sandbox launch inside another sandbox work — tests that need either are skipped in a confined run instead.
Changing the confined-session sandbox policy itself (the `/tmp` deny, the run temp roots, network rules) — this spec makes tests fit the policy, never the reverse.
Running the confined runner over `test/ui/` or `test/e2e/` — only `test/unit/` and `test/integration/` are covered.
A static lint for literal `/tmp/` strings in tests — most such strings are harmless path values that are never written; the confined CI run is the gate.
Moving test fixtures into `.nax/scratchpad/` — the scratchpad is the agent's own notes space; tests use `$TMPDIR` through `makeTempDir()`.
Changing `reviewerCommandsSection()` or any pipeline-mode (non-workflow) reviewer prompt.
Feeding the confined runner's result into nax's own run gates or the workflow `full-suite` gate — it is a CI and developer gate only.
An LLM or fuzzy-match dedupe of re-review new findings — only the exact file-and-line match against a `PARTIAL` residual is dropped.
Splitting `inputTokens` into cached and uncached parts, or changing cost computation — the cache fields are additive telemetry.
Cache token columns in the cost ledger, `run.complete` or metrics files other than the workflow role table and its summary line.
Log lines for `workflow.publish` mode `none`, and progress lines for the ledger commit and ledger push.
Configuring the CI-wait heartbeat interval — it is the constant `CI_WAIT_HEARTBEAT_MS`.
Including the gate command lines in the review prompts — the story gate record holds states, not commands.
